主要内容: MillerCoors and Pabst Brewing are set to go to trial in November over a half-a-billion-dollar lawsuit filed by Pabst against the Keystone beer maker. The dispute centers on a decades-old brewing agreement under which MillerCoors brews all of Pabst's legacy beers, including Pabst Blue Ribbon. The contract is set to expire in 2020, with two options to renew. MillerCoors has argued it may not have the capacity to continue the relationship due to declining U.S. volume. Pabst claims the contract renewal is crucial to avoid orphaning its beer brands, as building a brewery for Pabst's scale is expensive and rare. Pabst is accusing MillerCoors of breach of contract, anti-competition laws, fraud, and misrepresentation, while MillerCoors contests these claims, asserting it has the right to determine its capacity. A Milwaukee court judge denied MillerCoors' motion for summary judgment in April, allowing the case to proceed to trial. MillerCoors, owned by Molson Coors, reported a 12.2% drop in EBITDA and a 3.8% decline in volume in its last quarter. The judge also raised questions about the potential closure of a MillerCoors brewery in Irwindale, California, following the closure of one in Eden, North Carolina in 2016. MillerCoors argues that the potential closure may impact its capacity to brew Pabst beers, thus justifying not renewing the contract. The legal battle between MillerCoors and Pabst Brewing is set to go to trial in November. The case centers around potential brewery closures and business strategies. In a court filing, the judge noted that MillerCoors' current CEO stated the company would remain flat in 2018 and achieve growth in 2019. This raised questions about whether the company would need to close its second brewery. However, the judge also mentioned there is no official decision by the board to close the second brewery. A MillerCoors spokesperson told CNBC, "We routinely evaluate our brewery footprint, our capacity, and our efficiency as a matter of smart business. We are not planning to close Irwindale or any other brewery at this time." Pabst Brewing declined to comment on the matter.
